body:
ACCEPT D3 AS A HARD CONSTRAINT — and make it an artifact law, not a styling promise.

Measured basis: ADR 0002 already commits D4 no view-side inference, D9 typed uncertainty, D11 separate coverage/missingness masks, D12 a deterministic textual twin, and V-U1 missingness distinct from zero. Current view.FeatureChannelState proves part of the necessary shape with NotRequested, Unresolved, Missing, and SidecarRequired, and AtlasTextualTwin prints that state independently of observation count. But the current view foundation does not yet constitute a complete Measured/Absent/Imputed/Ineligible display contract. So I agree with D3 and would sharpen it this way:

FOR EVERY REQUESTED CHANNEL, THE BUNDLE MUST DECLARE THE ELIGIBLE UNIVERSE AND ACCOUNT FOR EVERY MEMBER AS MEASURED, ABSENT, IMPUTED, INELIGIBLE, UNRESOLVED/FAILED, OR EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED. No rendered silence may carry one of those meanings by convention.

That denominator clause matters. A picture cannot make absence visible if the artifact never says what was eligible to be present. It also preserves ADR 0002 D4: we may render a recorded absence or unresolved acquisition, but must not infer absence from the lack of a mark.

I would require three linked courts:
1. Zero versus missing: an eligible measured numeric zero remains a measured mark; it cannot become the missing glyph or disappear.
2. Not-requested versus ineligible versus failed: all three yield distinct textual-twin and non-colour visual states, even if none has a numeric sidecar row.
3. Suppression mutation: delete one eligible observation from the lowering input without updating the accounting manifest; compilation/lowering must refuse, not silently emit a cleaner picture.

The non-colour rule needs to apply locally, not only in a legend: pattern/shape/line grammar plus text or accessible label at the affected target. An artifact-level gap table is legitimate when no honest span anchor exists; inventing a span merely to place a missingness glyph would violate D4.

D1: hard ACCEPT standoff. Preserve the exact input bytes as source.txt, bind them by checksum, and express support as offsets into that immutable byte/text axis. Inline can be a lossy convenience export only; it cannot be canonical identity.

D2 and D5 together: split interchange from report. model.json should be the canonical, versioned, round-trippable semantic artifact (decode to Draft, revalidate; receipt and sidecar identities explicit). preview.html is a deterministic report over that artifact and owes source/checksum/view/config receipts plus its textual twin; it does not owe parse(HTML) == model. This avoids making layout geometry part of model identity while still giving the CLI an honest interchange output. A brat exporter can be useful, but its loss manifest must name dropped distinctions and bind the source/model checksum.

D4: do not make one overlay solve two incompatible reading tasks. The Codex text rail is the canonical span/evidence view. A sibling Atlas panel is the relation/hierarchy view; synchronize them by Address/AnnotationId/MarkId as ADR 0002 already requires. Cross-page causal/world-time edges should resolve into paired portal endpoints plus a relation inventory, not a giant arc pretending pagination is semantic geometry.

Minimal bundle I would converge on:
- source.txt — byte-identical input
- model.json — canonical standoff semantics and receipts
- preview.html — self-contained, script-free report if current StoryAtlas contract permits
- receipt.json — exact source/model/view/layout/software identities
- optional export-loss.json plus lossy .ann

Acceptance should compare all four identities and prove the HTML text rail reconstructs source.txt exactly. WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not inspect the sibling StoryAtlas checkout in this pass, design wire vocabulary, create a bead, or authorize implementation. This is a disposition on the format boundary from current storymodel4s ADR/source contracts.
